papers.t: Rare primary bilateral ovarian myeloid sarcoma preceding acute myeloid leukemia: ovarian-sparing management with long-term ovarian function and pregnancy after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation-a case report
papers.c: This case highlights the diagnostic limitations of imaging for atypical ovarian masses, the importance of intraoperative reassessment, and that individualized fertility-conserving management may achieve favorable oncologic and reproductive outcomes in selected young women.
ab: Background

Myeloid sarcoma is a rare extramedullary manifestation of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) that may mimic benign gynecologic disease and delay diagnosis. Ovarian involvement is particularly uncommon, with bilateral disease rarely reported.
Case

We describe a 24-year-old nulliparous woman presenting with dysmenorrhea, chronic pelvic pain and bilateral adnexal masses suggestive of endometrioma on ultrasonography. Laparoscopy demonstrated bilaterally enlarged predominantly solid ovaries inconsistent with the preoperative diagnosis. Fertility-conserving surgery with unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and contralateral ovarian conservation was performed because of the patient's young age, reproductive goals and uncertain diagnosis. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry confirmed myeloid sarcoma with variable membranous positive for CD45 and strong positivity for myeloperoxidase, and CD117. Initial peripheral blood smear was normal; however, AML with t(8;21) and RUNX1-RUNX1T1 fusion developed 50 days later. The patient subsequently underwent cytarabine-based chemotherapy followed by allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. At 60-month follow-up, she remains in complete remission with restoration of ovarian function, evidenced by regular menstrual cycles and normal anti-Müllerian hormone levels. She subsequently underwent in vitro fertilization using her own eggs and successfully conceived.
Conclusion

This case highlights the diagnostic limitations of imaging for atypical ovarian masses, the importance of intraoperative reassessment, and that individualized fertility-conserving management may achieve favorable oncologic and reproductive outcomes in selected young women.

papers.t: Increase in fetal haemoglobin from baseline to day 10 is a biomarker for response to decitabine in AML: Results of the AML21 randomized phase III trial of the EORTC Leukemia Group, Gruppo Italiano Malattie Ematologiche dell'Adulto (GIMEMA) and German MDS Study Group
papers.c: Baseline HbF in the decitabine arm was not associated with CR/CRi (OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.45-1.75, p = 0.73) or overall survival (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.58-1.28, p = 0.47). In conclusion, this large prospective study adds to the body of evidence that HbF is an easy-to-measure early biomarker for response to HMA treatment.
ab: Lack of response or delayed response to therapy are major challenges in the use of DNA-hypomethylating agents (HMA) in patients with acute myeloid leukaemia (AML). Fetal haemoglobin (HbF) is a potential biomarker for response to HMA treatment but has only been studied in small single-centre studies. We investigated the association between HbF and treatment outcome in the randomized phase 3 European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC)-1301 trial AML21, which included 606 fit, older AML patients who received 10-day decitabine or '3 + 7' chemotherapy as induction. HbF was measured twice in the decitabine arm (n = 135) and at baseline in the 3 + 7 arm (n = 97). In the decitabine arm, HbF increase from baseline to day 10 was associated with increased odds of reaching complete remission (CR) or CR with incomplete count recovery (CRi) (odds ratio [OR] 2.40, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.15-5.02, p = 0.020). The hazard ratio (HR) for death comparing patients with HbF increase to those without was 0.83 (95% CI 0.55-1.28, p = 0.40). Baseline HbF in the decitabine arm was not associated with CR/CRi (OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.45-1.75, p = 0.73) or overall survival (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.58-1.28, p = 0.47). In conclusion, this large prospective study adds to the body of evidence that HbF is an easy-to-measure early biomarker for response to HMA treatment.

papers.t: Environmental risk factors for acute myeloid leukemia in adults, a systematic review
papers.c: A limited number of studies have addressed the risk of AML associated with environmental exposure. Overall conclusions based on the existing evidence are not possible, as nearly half of the eligible studies had a high RoB, study estimates varied considerably, and a limited number of studies were available within each exposure category.
ab: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) is an aggressive hematologic cancer affected by various risk factors. Currently, the knowledge regarding the risk of AML associated with general environmental factors is limited. In a systematic review, we aimed to investigate the existing evidence. A literature search in three databases was initially conducted on May 24, 2024, and updated throughout the study period with a finale search on November 26, 2025. Studies were screened by title and abstract (n = 6685) and by full-text reading (n = 133). The quality of all included studies was evaluated by a risk-of-bias (RoB) tool and the certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. No meta-analysis was performed. The review revealed that 15 studies met the inclusion criteria representing 11 independent study populations. Seven studies were rated with a high RoB, five with moderate RoB and three with low RoB. Associations without high RoB were only observed in four studies, and related to air pollution (PM2.5, BC, SIA, NH4, NOx and NO3) and farm residency. The overall certainty of evidence was evaluated across exposure categories and found that air pollution had a low certainty, whereas residential benzene exposure, farm residency, chlorinated drinking water, radiation, residential proximity to industries, and living near power lines all had a very low certainty. A limited number of studies have addressed the risk of AML associated with environmental exposure. Overall conclusions based on the existing evidence are not possible, as nearly half of the eligible studies had a high RoB, study estimates varied considerably, and a limited number of studies were available within each exposure category.

papers.t: Risk-Adapted Donor Selection in Patients with Acute Myeloid Leukemia
papers.c: MUD was associated with better OS than alternative donors (MMUD and HID) through lower NRM, and its survival benefit was largest in high-risk disease. Donor selection in AML can be risk-adapted: MUD could be prioritized in high-risk disease, whereas GRFS should guide donor choice in lower-risk disease, where OS is similar across donor types.
ab: Background

The optimal donor for adults with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who lack a matched sibling donor (MSD) remains uncertain in Asian practice, where antithymocyte globulin (ATG)-based graft-versus-host disease (GvHD) prophylaxis is common.
Objectives

To compare outcomes after MSD, matched unrelated donor (MUD), mismatched unrelated donor (MMUD), and haploidentical donor (HID) transplantation, and to test whether disease risk modifies the donor effect.
Study Design

We analyzed 1,963 adults with AML who underwent first allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) in the Taiwan Blood and Marrow Transplantation Registry between 2009 and 2025. We applied a doubly robust strategy combining multinomial propensity-score inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) with multivariable Cox and Fine-Gray regression. GvHD was evaluated as a mediator by landmark and causal mediation analyses.
Results

Using MUD as reference, all three other donor types had inferior overall survival (OS), reaching significance for HID (hazard ratio [HR] 1.34, p=0.022) and MMUD (HR 1.31, p=0.026) but not for MSD (HR 1.18, p=0.131). Non-relapse mortality (NRM) was higher after HID (HR 1.61, p=0.011), with a trend after MMUD (HR 1.38, p=0.079), and GvHD-free, relapse-free survival (GRFS) was inferior after MSD (HR 1.40, p<0.001) and HID (HR 1.31, p=0.008). Relapse did not differ by donor type, indicating that the survival advantage of MUD operates through lower NRM. Causal mediation analysis did not attribute the MUD-HID survival difference to GvHD. Disease risk modified the donor effect on OS (interaction p=0.028). In high/very-high-risk disease, MUD was superior to MSD, MMUD, and HID (HR 1.44, 1.78, and 1.74, respectively), with 3-year OS of 42.7% after MUD and 28.5% after other donors. In low/intermediate-risk disease, OS did not differ by donor type.
Conclusions

MUD was associated with better OS than alternative donors (MMUD and HID) through lower NRM, and its survival benefit was largest in high-risk disease. Donor selection in AML can be risk-adapted: MUD could be prioritized in high-risk disease, whereas GRFS should guide donor choice in lower-risk disease, where OS is similar across donor types.

papers.t: Luspatercept in Myelodysplastic Syndromes With Ring Sideroblasts: Long Term Outcome and Impact on Non-Erythroid Blood Counts
papers.c: Decreasing evaluable sample sizes and the retrospective design limit interpretation. Associations with survival and non-erythroid blood counts require confirmation and should not be interpreted as causal effects.
ab: Long-term real-world data on Luspatercept (Luspa) in lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes with ring sideroblasts (MDS-RS) and transfusion-dependent anemia (RBC-TD) who are refractory or ineligible to erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) remain limited. Despite evidence of efficacy from clinical trials and real-world studies, long-term data in routine clinical practice are scarce, particularly regarding its effects on non-erythroid lineages. Furthermore, there is currently no consensus on the total duration of treatment, especially in non-responding cases. Thus, we analyzed 48 patients with low-risk MDS-RS treated with Luspa for ESA-refractory RBC-TD. Response was assessed at 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years according to International Working Group (IWG) 2018 criteria. At 6 months, 23/42 (54.8%) and 15/42 (35.7%) patients reached a response and transfusion independence, respectively. At 1 year, 16/30 (53.3%) patients showed a response, including 12 who already responded at 6 months. At 2 years, 10/20 (50%) patients maintained response and 2/20 (10%) were de novo responders. Treatment was well tolerated, with no significant adverse events reported; 21 (43.8%) patients discontinued Luspa, principally due to lack of response. After a median follow-up of 29.8 months (95% CI: 24.4-35.2), 6-month responders had longer overall survival in a landmark analysis. Exploratory analyses identified associations of 6-month response with additional somatic mutations and the SF3B1 hotspot mutation, the latter retained in the multivariable model; monocyte count was associated with 2-year response. Neutrophil counts significantly increased at 1 year compared with baseline, while platelet counts remained stable. Intriguingly, monocytes were increased at the three time points compared to baseline. Specifically, long-term responders presented higher levels of neutrophils and monocytes, as well decreased level of LDH, compared with non-responders. Responses were observed during long-term treatment, mainly in patients who had responded at earlier assessments. Decreasing evaluable sample sizes and the retrospective design limit interpretation. Associations with survival and non-erythroid blood counts require confirmation and should not be interpreted as causal effects.

papers.t: Impact of Venetoclax Bridging on Haematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation Outcomes in Advanced Myelodysplastic Neoplasms
papers.c: In this cohort, no clear post-transplant outcome benefit was observed with VEN-HMA bridging. The association with inferior RFS warrants further investigation but does not establish a causal adverse effect of VEN exposure.
ab: Background

Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) is the only curative therapy for higher-risk myelodysplastic neoplasms (HR-MDS), defined here as MDS with increased blasts (MDS-IB1/IB2). Whether venetoclax plus a hypomethylating agent (VEN-HMA) improves post-transplant outcomes when used as pre-transplant bridging is uncertain.
Study Design

We retrospectively analyzed 240 patients with MDS-IB1/IB2 undergoing first allo-HSCT (2020-2024), stratified by pre-transplant strategy: best supportive care (BSC, n=124), cytoreductive therapy (CYT, n=79), or VEN-HMA bridging (VEN, n=37). Median age was 47 years; 85% had higher-risk IPSS-M. Outcomes were compared by Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, IPSS-M, diagnostic blast percentage, HCT-CI, donor type, conditioning intensity and transplant year, and by propensity-score matching (PSM) with a 1:2 target ratio.
Results

Two-year OS was 94.0% (BSC), 88.4% (CYT) and 82.3% (VEN); 2-year RFS was 89.0%, 79.4% and 71.6%. In univariate analysis, VEN was associated with inferior OS (HR 3.11, 95% CI 1.05-9.22; P=0.041) and RFS (HR 2.61, 95% CI 1.16-5.86; P=0.020) versus BSC. In the primary Firth-penalized Cox analysis using Wald inference, VEN-HMA was associated with inferior RFS (HR 2.54, 95% CI 1.04-6.18, P=0.040), whereas the adjusted OS estimate was imprecise (HR 2.96, 95% CI 0.90-9.75; P=0.075). In supportive propensity-score-matched analysis incorporating selected molecular and cytogenetic covariates, the RFS hazard ratio for VEN-HMA versus BSC was 1.88 (95% CI 0.63-5.64; P=0.259), with residual covariate imbalance. The 2-year cumulative incidence of NRM was 4.2% (BSC), 2.7% (CYT) and 14.3% (VEN) (three-group Gray's P=0.054).
Conclusions

In this cohort, no clear post-transplant outcome benefit was observed with VEN-HMA bridging. The association with inferior RFS warrants further investigation but does not establish a causal adverse effect of VEN exposure.

papers.t: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors are associated with reduced AML transformation in systemic mastocytosis with myeloid neoplasm
papers.c: In an international registry analysis of 201 patients with SM-AHN, KIT D816V-selective TKI exposure was associated with longer overall survival (37.9 vs 17.8 months; P <.001) and lower 36-month incidence of acute myeloid leukemia transformation (5.9% vs 27.1%; P <.001).

papers.t: BCL11B-activated pediatric acute myeloid leukemia: a high-risk disease with frequent induction failure

Frequent FLT3 and IDH co-mutations in acute myeloid leukemia with mutated NPM1, NUP98 rearrangement, and KMT2A partial tandem duplication but not rearrangement: potential for combined targeted therapy
Distinct clinical and molecular profiles of acute myeloid leukemia defined by mutations in IDH1, IDH2, and TET2
papers.c: The mutational groups also showed distinct closest normal counterparts among healthy hematopoietic cell populations. Together, these findings demonstrate that IDH1, IDH2, and TET2 mutations define clinically and molecularly distinct subgroups of AML, highlighting the relevance of mutation-specific clinical stratification.
ab: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a heterogeneous disease driven by recurring somatic mutations, frequently affecting genes involved in epigenetic regulation. Mutations in IDH1, IDH2, and TET2 are largely mutually exclusive and thought to converge on a shared pathway by impairing TET-mediated DNA demethylation, either directly through loss of TET2 activity or indirectly through the accumulation of the oncometabolite (R)-2-hydroxyglutarate (2-HG) in IDH1- and IDH2-mutant AML. Whether this biochemical convergence translates into similar disease biology remains unclear. Here, we analyzed AML defined by mutations in IDH1, IDH2, or TET2 using population-based data from the Swedish AML Registry, complemented by transcriptomic and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) profiling of purified blasts from a highly selected subset of primary AML samples. TET2-mutant AML occurred at an older age and was associated with a more pronounced thrombocytopenia, whereas IDH1- and IDH2-mutant AML showed deeper neutropenia and more favorable overall survival, including after adjustment for clinical covariates. Transcriptomic and 5hmC alterations showed only modest concordance, with 5hmC profiles providing clearer separation of the mutational subgroups. TET2-mutant samples showed significant enrichment of the oxidative phosphorylation pathway compared with IDH1- and IDH2-mutant AML. The mutational groups also showed distinct closest normal counterparts among healthy hematopoietic cell populations. Together, these findings demonstrate that IDH1, IDH2, and TET2 mutations define clinically and molecularly distinct subgroups of AML, highlighting the relevance of mutation-specific clinical stratification.

papers.t: Salvage-free, transplantation-free survival: a proposal for a new clinical endpoint in acute myeloid leukemia
papers.c: In the prospective randomized ALFA-0701 trial, gemtuzumab ozogamycin significantly improved STFS. STFS should complement other survival endpoints to accurately analyze the impact of new drugs in AML.
ab: Results from pivotal clinical trials evaluating the combination of intensive chemotherapy with targeted therapies in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) are expected soon. While overall survival (OS) or event-free survival (EFS) are the recommended endpoints, new criteria are needed for assessing the intrinsic effectiveness of new drugs. In this study, the salvage-free, transplantation-free survival (STFS) was measured from day 1 of induction chemotherapy to the date of induction failure or salvage therapy, allogeneic transplantation (allo-HSCT), relapse, or death from any cause, whichever occurs first and assessed in a cohort of 1966 AML patients from the DATAML registry treated with intensive chemotherapy and 100 acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) patients treated with arsenic trioxide and all-trans retinoic acid. Validation cohorts from the ALFA group were used. At five years, STFS was estimated at 14.6% (95% confidence interval [CI], 13.0-16.2; median, 5.5 months) whereas OS, EFS and relapse-free survival estimations were 40.4% (95% CI, 38.2-42.6; median, 30.6 months), 31.4% (95% CI, 29.4-33.5; median, 15.3 months) and 37.6% (95% CI, 35.2-40.0; median, 21.9 months), respectively. Relapse was the most common first STFS event, followed by allo-HSCT. STFS varied depending on molecular subgroups and gene-gene mutation interactions. In the APL cohort, STFS (83.6% at five years) was similar to OS (85.6%) illustrating the impact of an effective and low-toxicity first-line treatment curing patients without salvage therapy or allo-HSCT. In the prospective randomized ALFA-0701 trial, gemtuzumab ozogamycin significantly improved STFS. STFS should complement other survival endpoints to accurately analyze the impact of new drugs in AML.

papers.t: Frontline isocitrate dehydrogenase inhibitor therapy in isocitrate dehydrogenase-mutated myelodysplastic neoplasms
Reply to: "Interpreting the Association Between Plasma Citrulline and Bloodstream Infection in Pediatric Acute Myeloid Leukemia"
Refining the boundary between myelodysplastic neoplasm and chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia under World Health Organization 2022 criteria using open-source data
Temporal Trends in Real-World Outcomes With CPX-351 in Secondary/High-Risk Acute Myeloid Leukemia: A PETHEMA Study
papers.c: Only TP53 wild-type status [HR 0.51 (95% CI: 0.25-1.05)] and achievement of MRD negativity after induction [HR 0.54 (95% CI: 0.29-1.0)] remained independently associated with improved OS. Overall, outcomes after CPX-351 appeared to improve over time in unadjusted analyses; however, the absence of an independent effect of treatment period and differences in patient selection between periods preclude attributing this improvement specifically to a temporal learning effect.
ab: CPX-351, a liposomal formulation of cytarabine and daunorubicin, has been approved patients with secondary/high-risk acute myeloid leukemia including therapy-related acute myeloid leukemia or AML with myelodysplasia-related changes according to the WHO 2016 classification. The aim of this study was to determine the efficacy and safety of CPX-351 in 283 patients with AML registered in the PETHEMA database. Evolving outcome results were analyzed comparing early treated patients (before-2022, N = 147) with those treated after Spanish financial approval (since-2022, N = 136). The CR/CRi rate was 54% in the overall cohort, without significant differences comparing both time periods. By contrast, early death rates at day + 30 and day + 60 were higher in early period patients (11.6 vs. 5.1% and 17 vs. 8.1%, p = 0.03 and p = 0.031). Consequently, more patients could undergo HSCT in the latter treatment period (33.8% vs. 25.2%, p = 0.04). Patients treated with CPX-351 since 2022 showed a significantly higher unadjusted 2-year OS probability compared with patients treated earlier [40.3% (95% CI: 26.3-62.4) versus 25.2% (95% CI: 18.6-34.1), P = 0.017]. However, treatment period was not independently associated with OS in multivariable analysis. Only TP53 wild-type status [HR 0.51 (95% CI: 0.25-1.05)] and achievement of MRD negativity after induction [HR 0.54 (95% CI: 0.29-1.0)] remained independently associated with improved OS. Overall, outcomes after CPX-351 appeared to improve over time in unadjusted analyses; however, the absence of an independent effect of treatment period and differences in patient selection between periods preclude attributing this improvement specifically to a temporal learning effect.

papers.t: Improved multistate survival in younger AML patients over time
papers.c: Increased CR rates and an increased application of alloHSCT mainly accounted for improved MS and OS. MS, as a novel endpoint, effectively captures favorable treatment outcome, while allowing quantification of the survival gain of pivotal, subsequent intermediate states.
ab: Over the last three decades, HOVON-SAKK has performed six randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in newly diagnosed younger adults with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). While overall survival (OS) improved over time, no OS benefit was apparent in individual RCTs. We investigated whether complete remission (CR) rates, postremission treatment (PRT), and/or a reduction of early mortality might have accounted for improved OS. Two multistate models, from the start of induction treatment until the date of death or last contact, were developed. These models included (1) CR ≤ 2 cycles and (2) CR followed by type of PRT as intermediate states and overall mortality as an end state. Patients were categorized by decade of diagnosis. Transition probabilities were adjusted for age and European LeukemiaNet (ELN) 2017 risk classification. Multistate survival (MS) was defined by the probability of obtaining CR with the intention or actual receipt of PRT and surviving thereafter. A total of 924, 1896, and 2253 patients were enrolled between 1987-1996, 1997-2006, and 2007-2017, respectively. OS at 5 years increased from 33 ± 2% to 47 ± 1% in the most recent cohort. CR rates increased from 77.5% to 83.9%. Sixty-day mortality decreased from 9.9% to 7.8%. The proportion of alloHSCT as PRT increased from 16.6% to 48.3%. MS at 5 years increased from 28.8% to 47.4% and from 11.3% to 26.1% for ELN17 intermediate and adverse risk patients, which was largely due to improved OS in CR patients proceeding to alloHSCT. Increased CR rates and an increased application of alloHSCT mainly accounted for improved MS and OS. MS, as a novel endpoint, effectively captures favorable treatment outcome, while allowing quantification of the survival gain of pivotal, subsequent intermediate states.

papers.t: Post-transplant maintenance in acute myeloid leukemia in Italy: results of the GITMO-maintenance survey
Measurable Residual Disease in IDH-Mutated AML: Identifying a Clinically Relevant Threshold for IDH Mutation Monitoring
papers.c: A 0.2% VAF threshold was associated with clinically distinct outcomes and may provide a useful framework for IDH-based MRD assessment in AML.
ab: Background

Isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutations are recurrent in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and represent promising targets for measurable residual disease (MRD) monitoring. However, clinically validated strategies for IDH-based MRD assessment remain lacking.
Methods

We evaluated the analytical performance and clinical utility of droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) for IDH mutation monitoring in a single-center cohort of patients with IDH-mutated AML treated with curative intent. Healthy controls were included to characterize low-level background signals and identify a clinical threshold.
Results

ddPCR showed robust analytical performance, with a limit of detection of 0.01% variant allele frequency (VAF) and strong concordance with NGS. Low-level IDH mutation signals were frequently detected in healthy individuals and in patients in remission. We identified 0.2% VAF as a candidate threshold for clinically relevant IDH MRD. Using this cutoff, post-treatment detectable IDH MRD was associated with a higher 2-year cumulative incidence of relapse (63.6% vs. 20%; p = 0.019) and inferior overall survival (70.6% vs. 92.9%; p = 0.04). Among patients negative by multiparameter flow cytometry, ddPCR identified residual IDH-mutated clones in 56% of cases, who showed higher relapse rates than double-negative patients (50% vs. 0%; p = 0.031).
Conclusions
A 0.2% VAF threshold was associated with clinically distinct outcomes and may provide a useful framework for IDH-based MRD assessment in AML.

papers.t: Identification of a Novel KRAS::ETNK1 Fusion Transcript in a Myelodysplastic/Myeloproliferative Overlap Syndrome With Eosinophilia: A Case Report
papers.c: This case provides new insights into rare genetic alterations in MDS/MPN, possible mechanisms of immune-mediated clonal selection after allogeneic stem cell transplantation, and the dynamics of leukemic evolution. Trial Registration: The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.
ab: This work describes, to our knowledge, the first reported case of a patient with an MDS/MPN overlap syndrome harboring a novel KRAS::ETNK1 fusion transcript. The disease initially presented with eosinophilia, megakaryocyte expansion, mast cell infiltration, and a background of typical MDS/MPN-associated mutations (ASXL1, TET2, EZH2, BCOR, and SETBP1). Following allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, the fusion-bearing clone disappeared due to a chromosome 12p deletion, and the disease evolved into secondary AML with distinct molecular drivers (MYB, EP300, FAT1, and GATA2). This case provides new insights into rare genetic alterations in MDS/MPN, possible mechanisms of immune-mediated clonal selection after allogeneic stem cell transplantation, and the dynamics of leukemic evolution. Trial Registration: The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

papers.t: Bosmolisib (BR101801), a novel PI3K-δ/γ and DNA-PK inhibitor for relapsed/refractory patients with peripheral T-cell lymphoma: a phase I study
papers.c: Pharmacodynamics profiling showed statistically significant decrease in regulatory T-cells. These findings support evaluation of bosmolisib in a phase 2 trial (ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04018248).
ab: Bosmolisib is a novel triple inhibitor of PI3K-δ/γ and DNA-PK for malignancy treatment. This was a first-in-human, phase 1, open-label, dose-escalation, and dose-expansion trial with relapsed/refractory (R/R) non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL). Patients received bosmolisib orally once daily in 28-day cycles across four dose levels (50-325 mg) until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The study utilized a 3 + 3 dose-escalation design to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D), followed by expansion at RP2D. Primary endpoints were safety and MTD/RP2D determination; secondary endpoints included efficacy, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics. A total of 26 patients were enrolled in dose-escalation (N = 12) and dose-expansion (N = 14). Median age was 65 years with a median of 3 prior therapies. Bosmolisib demonstrated acceptable tolerability; dose-limiting toxicities were observed at 325 mg (alanine transaminase [ALT] increased and erythema multiforme), establishing MTD/RP2D at 200 mg. Most adverse events (AEs) were Grade 1-2, with the most common Grade ≥3 AEs (ALT 23.1%, aspartate transaminase 15.4%). Of 23 evaluable patients, the overall response rate (ORR) was 26.1%, and in PTCL patients, ORR was 31.6% with one patient achieving a durable complete response. Pharmacodynamics profiling showed statistically significant decrease in regulatory T-cells. These findings support evaluation of bosmolisib in a phase 2 trial (ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04018248).

papers.t: A multi-center, single-arm, phase 2 trial of dasatinib in T follicular helper cell lymphomas
papers.c: Conversely, early progression correlates with a high TET2 mutation burden in non-malignant immune cells, including CD8+ T cell subsets. While the primary outcome is below the prespecified endpoint, our exploratory findings implicate immune dysfunction involving TET2 mutations in limiting the therapeutic benefit of dasatinib.
ab: T follicular helper cell lymphomas (TFHL) harbor activating T cell receptor (TCR) signaling mutations and epigenetic alterations, such as TET2 mutations. Here, we conduct a multi-center, single-arm, phase 2 trial of the tyrosine kinase inhibitor dasatinib in patients with relapsed/refractory TFHLs (jRCT2031190079). The primary outcome is the overall response rate (ORR) according to CT-based Lugano criteria 2014. Key secondary endpoints include ORR in RHOA-mutated patients and progression-free/overall survival. The main inclusion criteria consist of TFHL diagnosis and relapse following at least 1 prior chemotherapy regimen. Key exclusion criteria encompass central nervous system involvement, history of other malignancies, and receipt of chemotherapy or radiotherapy within 4 weeks. Nineteen patients are enrolled, with 18 receiving dasatinib and 17 evaluable for efficacy. Median age is 73 years, 50% are female, and angioimmunoblastic T cell lymphoma is the predominant subtype (n = 13). Dasatinib yields a 23.5% ORR, below the prespecified 30% endpoint. Treatment-related adverse events occur in 61.1% of patients (n = 11). Patients harboring TCR signaling mutations, especially those with RHOA p.G17V, achieve a 36.4% ORR, whereas no responses are observed in mutation-negative cases. Exploratory single-cell RNA sequencing reveals interferon-γ/tumor necrosis factor-enriched tumor microenvironments and peripheral expansion of cytotoxic T cell clones in responders. Conversely, early progression correlates with a high TET2 mutation burden in non-malignant immune cells, including CD8+ T cell subsets. While the primary outcome is below the prespecified endpoint, our exploratory findings implicate immune dysfunction involving TET2 mutations in limiting the therapeutic benefit of dasatinib.

papers.t: Patient-reported Outcomes in Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma Treated With Glofitamab Plus Gemcitabine and Oxaliplatin in STARGLO
papers.c: Glofit-GemOx maintained health-related quality of life and physical functioning, while providing earlier relief of pain and lymphoma symptoms versus R-GemOx. These findings align with the clinical benefits observed with Glofit-GemOx versus R-GemOx in STARGLO, further supporting Glofit-GemOx as a treatment option for relapsed/refractory DLBCL.
ab: Background

The phase III STARGLO study (NCT04408638) demonstrated an overall survival benefit with glofitamab plus gemcitabine and oxaliplatin (Glofit-GemOx) versus rituximab plus gemcitabine and oxaliplatin (R-GemOx) in transplant-ineligible relapsed/refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Here, the impact of treatment on patient-reported outcomes (PROs) in STARGLO was evaluated.
Materials And Methods

Patients were randomized 2:1 to Glofit-GemOx or R-GemOx. PROs were evaluated using the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30 and the Functional Assessment of Cancer Treatment-Lymphoma Lymphoma Subscale throughout treatment and follow-up. Endpoints included time to deterioration (TTD) and change from baseline in functioning and symptoms.
Results

Overall, 274 patients were enrolled (Glofit-GemOx, n = 183; R-GemOx, n = 91). PRO questionnaire response rates were 100% at baseline and > 90% on treatment. Baseline scores indicated moderate-to-high functioning and low-to-moderate symptom severity. Glofit-GemOx had nominal delays in median TTD versus R-GemOx for physical functioning (9.1 vs 8.2 months), fatigue (1.7 vs 1.4 months), and lymphoma symptoms (6.2 vs 4.5 months). Glofit-GemOx-treated patients achieved clinically meaningful improvements in pain and lymphoma symptoms earlier (by Cycle 3) than R-GemOx-treated patients. At end of treatment, pain improvements were maintained in Glofit-GemOx-treated patients, whereas scores for R-GemOx-treated patients returned to pre-treatment baseline.
Conclusion

Glofit-GemOx maintained health-related quality of life and physical functioning, while providing earlier relief of pain and lymphoma symptoms versus R-GemOx. These findings align with the clinical benefits observed with Glofit-GemOx versus R-GemOx in STARGLO, further supporting Glofit-GemOx as a treatment option for relapsed/refractory DLBCL.

papers.t: Proton pump inhibitors and outcome after axicabtagene ciloleucel for the treatment of non-Hodgkin B-cell lymphoma, a retrospective study with the DESCAR-T registry
Clinical outcomes of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia versus T-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation
papers.c: Overall, OS, DFS, CIR, NRM, and GRFS did not differ significantly between patients with T-ALL and T-LBL, although the effects of diagnosis on OS, DFS, CIR, and NRM changed during follow-up. These findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in larger multicenter studies.
ab: Although T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) and T-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma (T-LBL) were historically regarded as different manifestations of a single disease entity driven by immature T-lymphoblast proliferation, recent advances in molecular diagnostics and cytogenetic testing have revealed inherent differences in their molecular signatures and chromosomal profiles. Despite these differences, comparative data on clinical outcomes following allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) between the two subtypes remain limited. To address this gap, we retrospectively analyzed 106 consecutive patients, including 71 with T-ALL and 35 with T-LBL, who underwent allo-HSCT at our institution between January 2010 and January 2025. No statistically significant differences were observed in overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), graft-versus-host disease-free, relapse-free survival (GRFS), cumulative incidence of relapse (CIR), or cumulative incidence of non-relapse mortality (NRM) between patients with T-ALL and T-LBL. Diagnosis was not associated with these outcomes in multivariable analyses. However, the association between diagnosis and OS, DFS, CIR, and NRM varied over time. At 6 months, the multivariable analysis showed worse OS in T-LBL (hazard ratio at the specified time [HR(t)], 2.41; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.10-5.28; P = 0.028). At 36 months, T-LBL was associated with lower risks of DFS failure (HR(t), 0.16; 95% CI, 0.03-0.91; P = 0.039) and NRM (subdistribution hazard ratio at the specified time [sHR(t)], 0.06; 95% CI, 0.01-0.72; P = 0.026). The 36-month restricted mean survival time (RMST) for OS was 5.79 months shorter in T-LBL (95% CI, - 11.38 to - 0.19; P = 0.043), whereas DFS and GRFS RMST did not differ significantly. Results for most outcomes did not differ significantly between groups in either the PSM cohorts or the first complete remission subgroup, although moderate to severe chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) was less frequent in T-LBL. Complete case analyses for white blood cell (WBC) and lactic dehydrogenase (LDH) and analyses restricted to patients in complete remission with evaluable measurable residual disease (MRD) did not materially alter the diagnosis estimates. Overall, OS, DFS, CIR, NRM, and GRFS did not differ significantly between patients with T-ALL and T-LBL, although the effects of diagnosis on OS, DFS, CIR, and NRM changed during follow-up. These findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in larger multicenter studies.

papers.t: Management of advanced mycosis fungoides and Sézary Syndrome: International Recommendations for systemic treatments and allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation from the European Hematology Association, the EORTC Cutaneous Lymphoma Tumours Group, the International Society for Cutaneous Lymphoma, and the Lymphoma Working Party of the EBMT
papers.c: Practical treatment algorithms for advanced MF and SS are proposed to support therapeutic sequencing and multidisciplinary management. Allo-HCT remains the only potentially curative treatment and should be considered early in selected patients with high-risk disease features.
ab: Advanced mycosis fungoides (MF) and Sézary syndrome (SS) are the most aggressive forms of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and remain associated with a poor prognosis and heterogeneous therapeutic approaches. Recent advances, including targeted therapies and improved transplant strategies, have substantially expanded treatment options, highlighting the need for updated international guidance integrating dermatologic, hematologic, and transplant perspectives. An international multidisciplinary panel convened by the European Hematology Association (EHA), the EORTC Cutaneous Lymphoma Tumours Group (EORTC-CLTG), the International Society for Cutaneous Lymphoma (ISCL), and the EBMT Lymphoma Working Party reviewed the available evidence and developed consensus recommendations for the management of advanced MF and SS. Thirty international experts participated in the process. Recommendations address diagnostic work-up, systemic therapies, treatment sequencing, combination strategies, and indications for allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT). The consensus supports a stage-adapted and compartment-oriented therapeutic approach. Immunomodulatory strategies remain central in advanced CTCL: extracorporeal photopheresis is commonly used as first-line therapy in SS and in patients with significant blood involvement, while interferon-α and retinoids are widely used in MF, often in combination with skin-directed therapies. Mogamulizumab and brentuximab vedotin represent key options after prior systemic therapy, with differential activity across skin, blood, and nodal compartments. Combination approaches integrating systemic and skin-directed treatments may improve response depth and durability. Practical treatment algorithms for advanced MF and SS are proposed to support therapeutic sequencing and multidisciplinary management. Allo-HCT remains the only potentially curative treatment and should be considered early in selected patients with high-risk disease features.

papers.t: Projected population size by treatment line in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma in the United States, 2024-2028
papers.c: However, the projections were sensitive to the assumptions and values of certain inputs. The findings may support clinical sequencing decisions and inform future payer strategies in DLBCL management.
ab: Numerous novel therapies have emerged for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). This study used data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program and published efficacy estimates to project the number of adults in various DLBCL subpopulations on each line of therapy (LOT) from 2024 to 2028, accounting for potential new therapies. The projected average annual number of patients on first-line (1 L), second-line (2 L), and third-line (3 L) LOT was 30,404, 8,130, and 3,707, respectively, in the base case. The model predicted an increase in 1 L population over time, while the 2 L and 3 L populations were projected to increase initially and then decline, likely reflecting increased use of novel treatments in earlier lines. The trends were consistent across age groups and sensitivity analyses. However, the projections were sensitive to the assumptions and values of certain inputs. The findings may support clinical sequencing decisions and inform future payer strategies in DLBCL management.

papers.t: Quantitative and mutational properties in the ctDNA uncovered by systemic inflammation in large B-cell lymphoma
papers.c: We describe the added prognostic value of multimodal LB assessment, where patients with high levels of both ctDNA and inflammatory serum proteins have the worst overall survival (hazard ratio 7.93, p < 0.001) and progression free survival (hazard ratio 5.35, p < 0.001), thereby improving the risk estimate compared to either of the markers alone. This advanced multimodal LB employs clinically critical information on lymphoma and the host, both of which are essential for accurate treatment decision-making.
ab: Risk assessment of large B-cell lymphomas (LBCLs) using liquid biopsy (LB) has so far focused primarily on the genomic properties of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), overlooking the host response. We previously identified an inflamed serum protein signature that reflects systemic host response and correlates with survival. Here, we integrated the inflammation signature and ctDNA to connect inflammation to genomic alterations and defined how this crosstalk informs treatment outcomes in two independent LBCL cohorts from Nordic phase II trials. We identify initiation of immune evasion at multiple genomic levels in patients with an inflammatory serum profile and uncover distinct mutational signatures that reflect diagnostic subtypes and inflammatory host response. We describe the added prognostic value of multimodal LB assessment, where patients with high levels of both ctDNA and inflammatory serum proteins have the worst overall survival (hazard ratio 7.93, p < 0.001) and progression free survival (hazard ratio 5.35, p < 0.001), thereby improving the risk estimate compared to either of the markers alone. This advanced multimodal LB employs clinically critical information on lymphoma and the host, both of which are essential for accurate treatment decision-making.

papers.t: Primary bone lymphoma with cervical compression mimicking solitary osseous plasmacytoma
Follicular Lymphoma: 2027 Annual Update
papers.c: Targeted therapies, bispecific antibodies, and CAR-T cell therapies offer exciting new options for historically difficult-to-treat disease. Sequencing of novel therapies and their use earlier in treatment are areas of ongoing investigation. Recent data suggest FL may be cured in a portion of patients treated with chemoimmunotherapy. Minimal residual disease testing is a highly predictive test for progression and may have a role in FL management in the future.
ab: Background

Follicular lymphoma (FL) is the most common indolent lymphoma and has widely variable disease trajectories. While patients with a durable response to initial therapy have expected survival comparable to the general population, patients with early or recurrent relapses, or with transformation to large cell lymphoma, are at serious risk of lymphoma-associated death.
Summary
This review discusses the biological and clinical characteristics of FL as well as diagnostic assessment, prognostic tools, and treatment options.
Conclusion

Targeted therapies, bispecific antibodies, and CAR-T cell therapies offer exciting new options for historically difficult-to-treat disease. Sequencing of novel therapies and their use earlier in treatment are areas of ongoing investigation. Recent data suggest FL may be cured in a portion of patients treated with chemoimmunotherapy. Minimal residual disease testing is a highly predictive test for progression and may have a role in FL management in the future.

papers.t: Low tumor burden follicular lymphoma: The state of the art
papers.c: In this review, we synthesize the evidence underpinning current paradigms for front-line management decisions. We propose how the field can be advanced to optimize and individualize care for each patient to live longer and better with LTB FL.
ab: Follicular lymphoma (FL) is the commonest indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Most patients present with advanced-stage and are stratified by the Groupe d'Etude des Lymphomes Folliculaires (GELF) criteria into high or low tumor burden (LTB). Randomized trials in LTB FL demonstrated no overall survival advantage with immediate treatment compared to watchful waiting (WW). This led to the widespread practice of WW and the consideration of LTB FL as a single indolent continuum. However, LTB FL is heterogeneous, common, and understudied. Recent advances have led to renewed interest and a reconsideration of the optimal approach. Long-term data comparing rituximab to WW have recently been published providing an understanding of the benefits and limitations of each approach. Novel prognostic models have been developed to predict time to treatment to refine patient selection for WW. Advances in molecular biology have led to an improved understanding of FL lymphomagenesis. Circulating tumor DNA is being explored as a potential highly sensitive response assessment tool. These developments have renewed interest in the optimal approach to management. Early intervention trials with novel agents are currently exploring the hypotheses that LTB FL can be cured, altered, or transformation can be prevented in suitable patients. Conversely, WW remains an appropriate option. In this review, we synthesize the evidence underpinning current paradigms for front-line management decisions. We propose how the field can be advanced to optimize and individualize care for each patient to live longer and better with LTB FL.

papers.t: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy as a cure for large B-cell lymphoma
papers.c: Both studies show clear plateaus in Kaplan-Meier survival curves around 2 years, with sustained remissions extending to 5 years. These data offer a compelling perspective on the curative potential of CAR T-cell therapy while underscoring the need for continued follow‑up and broader analyses.
ab: Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL) is cured in most patients with first-line chemoimmunotherapy; however, 30%-40% of patients will have relapsed or refractory (R/R) disease. Of these patients, those with refractory or early relapsed LBCL may receive chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy as their second-line treatment if they are eligible, and those with late relapse may instead receive high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell transplantation, recently licensed second-line bispecific antibody with chemotherapy, other targeted agents, or palliative management only. This narrative review aims to summarize the data for CAR T-cell therapy as a curative-intent treatment for R/R LBCL based on available evidence. This evidence includes long‑term follow‑up data from the Phase 3 ZUMA‑7 and TRANSFORM trials, as well as other CAR T-cell therapy studies, which suggest the potential for CAR T‑cell therapy to achieve durable, possibly curative outcomes in R/R LBCL. Both studies show clear plateaus in Kaplan-Meier survival curves around 2 years, with sustained remissions extending to 5 years. These data offer a compelling perspective on the curative potential of CAR T-cell therapy while underscoring the need for continued follow‑up and broader analyses.

papers.t: The Histone Lactylation of KREMEN2 Inhibits Ferroptosis Through the JAK2/STAT3/GPX4 Axis and Promotes the Progression of Mantle Cell Lymphoma
papers.c: In vivo and in vitro experiments consistently demonstrated that inhibiting lactate production or knocking down KREMEN2 could inhibit tumor growth, and the combination of the two had a better effect. This study identifies a regulatory axis in MCL linking histone H3K18 lactylation to KREMEN2-mediated JAK2/STAT3/GPX4 pathway activation, providing a potential basis for developing targeted therapies against this disease.
ab: Mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) is an incurable B-cell tumor, and new therapeutic targets are urgently needed. This study demonstrates that kringle-containing transmembrane protein 2 (KREMEN2) is a key oncogenic factor in MCL. Mechanistically, lactate accumulated by abnormal tumor metabolism directly enhances the transcriptional expression of KREMEN2 by driving histone H3K18 lactylation (H3K18la). High expression of KREMEN2 further activates the Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3/Glutathione Peroxidase 4 (JAK2/STAT3/GPX4) signaling pathway to inhibit ferroptosis, and ultimately promotes malignant progression. Functionally, KREMEN2 knockdown induced ferroptosis and inhibited proliferation, and Erastin could not further induce ferroptosis in this state, demonstrating that KREMEN2 drove the progression of MCL by inhibiting the core ferroptotic phenotype. In addition, overexpression of downstream STAT3 can effectively reverse the phenotype caused by KREMEN2 knockdown. In vivo and in vitro experiments consistently demonstrated that inhibiting lactate production or knocking down KREMEN2 could inhibit tumor growth, and the combination of the two had a better effect. This study identifies a regulatory axis in MCL linking histone H3K18 lactylation to KREMEN2-mediated JAK2/STAT3/GPX4 pathway activation, providing a potential basis for developing targeted therapies against this disease.

papers.t: Baseline maximum standardised uptake value does not predict outcomes in high-tumour-burden follicular lymphoma treated with first-line immunochemotherapy
papers.c: Baseline maximum standardised uptake value does not predict survival in high-tumour-burden follicular lymphoma treated with first-line immunochemotherapy, but identifies patients at risk of histological transformation: no transformation occurred below the cohort median. Its role is to guide biopsy and surveillance rather than therapeutic stratification.

papers.t: Primary CNS lymphoma mimicking brain metastases with successful glucarpidase rescue and methotrexate rechallenge
The cyclin-G associated kinase (GAK) is a clinically actionable drug target required for mitosis in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
papers.c: GAK kinase function is therefore a targetable dependency, opening novel treatment strategies suitable for rapid clinical translation. Moreover, we establish phenotypic screening with target deconvolution as a generalizable strategy to reveal tumor-selective kinase dependencies.
ab: Though 100 kinase inhibitors are approved for clinical use, most kinases in the genome remain poorly characterized. Moreover, though kinase inhibitors have revolutionized the care of selected cancers, most others respond transiently or not at all to these drugs, typically directed against signal-transduction pathways. Given cellular regulation at every step by phosphorylation events, we hypothesized that phenotypic screening and machine-learning analysis can reveal novel kinase targets. Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), the most common lymphoma, responds poorly to signal transduction-directed kinase inhibitors. We applied a library of probes to DLBCL systems broadly representing its pathogenic heterogeneity and subjected results to iterative target-deconvolution analysis aimed at tumor selectivity (idTRAX). These efforts identified the cyclin G-associated kinase (GAK) as a tumor-selective target. Mechanistic studies showed GAK kinase activity is required for mitotic progression, with inhibition leading to G2/M arrest and cell death and increased efficacy in the absence of the retinoblastoma (RB) tumor suppressor. GAK-directed kinase inhibitors, including repurposed clinical compounds, showed promising single-agent anti-DLBCL activity in vivo. GAK kinase function is therefore a targetable dependency, opening novel treatment strategies suitable for rapid clinical translation. Moreover, we establish phenotypic screening with target deconvolution as a generalizable strategy to reveal tumor-selective kinase dependencies.

papers.t: Infections and their determinants in patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma receiving bispecific T-cell antibodies: Results from an international multicenter cohort study
Epcoritamab achieves durable remission after CD20 antigen escape in primary cardiac diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
papers.c: Epcoritamab has been continued for > 8 months without significant adverse events, and the patient remains in computed tomography scan confirmed complete remission. Based on this case, epcoritamab may retain clinically significant activity despite undetectable CD20 expression, and CD20 negativity alone should not automatically preclude its use in refractory DLBCL.
ab: CD20 antigen loss after anti-CD20-based therapy is a mechanism of immune escape in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Emerging real-world data have shown that patients with undetectable CD20 expression who are treated with CD20-targeting bispecific antibodies may have inferior outcomes. Herein, we report a 77-year-old female patient with primary cardiac DLBCL who exhibited cardiac tamponade. The patient's CD20 expression was weak based on immunohistochemistry but was clearly positive on flow cytometry (79.2%) upon diagnosis. She received dose-reduced rituximab, etoposide, prednisone, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, and doxorubicin, followed by polatuzumab vedotin plus rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and prednisone. However, she developed primary refractory disease with recurrent cardiac tamponade and embolic cerebral infarction, with near-complete loss of CD20 expression according to both immunohistochemistry and flow cytometry (0.1%) on rebiopsy. The patient was not eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy as she personally refused blood transfusions. After one cycle of salvage gemcitabine, carboplatin, and dexamethasone, epcoritamab therapy was initiated. Catecholamine support was discontinued on day 16 of cycle 1, and hemodynamic stability was achieved on day 22. Pericardial effusion completely resolved by the end of cycle 1. Epcoritamab has been continued for > 8 months without significant adverse events, and the patient remains in computed tomography scan confirmed complete remission. Based on this case, epcoritamab may retain clinically significant activity despite undetectable CD20 expression, and CD20 negativity alone should not automatically preclude its use in refractory DLBCL.

papers.t: An Open-label, Multicenter, Phase 2 Study to Assess the Safety and Efficacy of Burixafor (GPC-100) in Combination with Propranolol and G-CSF for the Mobilization of Hematopoietic Progenitor Cells in Multiple Myeloma Patients

Influence of CAR T-cell expansion and persistence in the peripheral blood on CAR T-cell therapy efficacy and adverse events in multiple myeloma
FcRH5-Targeted Therapy in Multiple Myeloma: Evolving Clinical Strategies and Resistance From IMS 2026

Multiple Myeloma in a Resource-Limited Setting: Clinical Presentation, Treatment Patterns, and Outcomes From a 99-Patient Cohort in Senegal
papers.c: These findings highlight persistent global disparities in MM care and underscore the urgent need for adapted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, and for strategies to reduce loss to follow-up, in low- and middle-income countries. Trial Registration: The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.
ab: Background: Therapeutic advances have profoundly improved outcomes in multiple myeloma (MM) in high-income countries. In sub-Saharan Africa; however, data remain scarce and access to novel therapies is limited. We aimed to characterize the clinical presentation, treatment strategies, and outcomes of MM patients managed in a resource-limited setting. Methods: We conduct a retrospective monocentric study including 99 patients diagnosed with MM according to International Myeloma Working Group (IMWG) criteria between 2011 and 2022 at the Hôpital Principal de Dakar. Clinical, biological, radiological, therapeutic, and outcome data were analyzed. Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and prognostic factors were assessed using univariable and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. Results: The mean age at diagnosis was 62.4 years, with a slight male predominance. Diagnosis was symptomatic in 86.9% of patients, mainly due to bone pain (62.6%). Advanced disease was common, with 68.7% presenting at Salmon-Durie stage III. Renal impairment and hypercalcemia were observed in 57.0% and 50.5% of cases, respectively. First-line treatment relied predominantly on conventional regimens (melphalan-prednison± thalidomide), while bortezomib-based therapies were used in only 11.1% of patients. After a median follow-up of 16 months, median OS was 73 months (95% CI: 23-NR) and median PFS was 31 months (95% CI: 23-NR); estimated OS was 60.0% at 12 months and 36.4% at 24 months. International Staging System (ISS) stage was the only independent predictor of OS (Stage III vs. Stage I: HR 13.4; 95% CI: 1.58-1755; p = 0.012). Nearly half of the cohort (49.5%) was lost to follow-up. Conclusions: In this Senegalese cohort, MM was diagnosed at an advanced stage and treated mainly with conventional regimens, resulting in poor survival outcomes compared with high-income settings. ISS stage was the strongest independent prognostic factor identified. These findings highlight persistent global disparities in MM care and underscore the urgent need for adapted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, and for strategies to reduce loss to follow-up, in low- and middle-income countries. Trial Registration: The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

papers.t: The impact of pomalidomide-containing induction on stem cell mobilization and engraftment in multiple myeloma: a single-center experience
papers.c: POM-containing induction reduces the likelihood of achieving optimal HSC collection targets and increases reliance on on-demand PXF, a negative impact further compounded by concomitant Dara use. Nonetheless, it does not preclude minimum dose collection or compromise long-term engraftment.
ab: Background

Autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) is the standard intensification therapy for eligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM) patients. While lenalidomide impairs hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) mobilization, data regarding pomalidomide (POM)-containing induction remain extremely limited.
Methods

This single-center, retrospective cohort study analyzed NDMM patients undergoing HSC mobilization with high-dose cyclophosphamide (CTX) plus pegylated granulocyte colony-stimulating factor between 2023 and 2025. A 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to balance baseline characteristics.
Results

From 111 patients initially included, 33 matched pairs (n = 66) were analyzed. The incidence of poor mobilization was similar between the POM and control groups (36.4% vs. 30.3%, P = 0.602). However, the POM group exhibited a marginally lower total CD34 + cell yield (median: 5.81 vs. 7.21 × 10⁶/kg, P = 0.059) and a significantly lower proportion of patients achieving the optimal target of ≥ 6 × 10⁶ cells/kg (45.5% vs. 72.7%, P = 0.024). Borderline increases in plerixafor (PXF) requirements (87.9% vs. 69.7%, P = 0.071) were observed with POM. Within the POM cohort, concomitant daratumumab (Dara) exposure significantly reduced total CD34 + yields (median: 5.19 vs. 8.24 × 10⁶/kg, P = 0.014) and increased PXF requirements (100.0% vs. 66.7%, P = 0.012). Post-ASCT engraftment kinetics were comparable (all P > 0.05).
Conclusions

POM-containing induction reduces the likelihood of achieving optimal HSC collection targets and increases reliance on on-demand PXF, a negative impact further compounded by concomitant Dara use. Nonetheless, it does not preclude minimum dose collection or compromise long-term engraftment.

papers.t: AI-Driven Structural Analysis Clarifies Novel TNFRSF17 Variants of Uncertain Significance as Candidate Resistance Mechanisms to BCMA-Targeted Immunotherapies in Multiple Myeloma
papers.c: Structural interpretation of TNFRSF17 variants may help prioritize newly identified variants for agent-specific functional evaluation. Direct disulfide-cysteine alterations were associated with broader predicted structural perturbation, non-cysteine variants more often showed agent-dependent effects. Prospective functional and clinical validation is required.
ab: Background

B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-directed immunotherapies have transformed care of relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (r/r MM), but most patients eventually progress. When whole-genome sequencing (WGS) at relapse reveals variants of uncertain significance (VUS) in the BCMA gene TNFRSF17, their functional significance and relevance to subsequent BCMA-directed therapy remain uncertain. We developed a structure-based framework to generate agent-level hypotheses of therapeutic binding after BCMA-directed therapy.
Methods

We analyzed a cohort of patients with r/r MM who underwent routine WGS at progression after BCMA-directed therapy at 2 German tertiary cancer centers; among the 25 evaluable samples, four non-truncating TNFRSF17 VUS were identified. These VUS were analyzed using a structure-informed framework to generate agent-specific predictions of preserved versus impaired therapeutic binding. Incremental discrimination was explored by comparison with direct disulfide-cysteine and agent-contact-only rules on experimentally labeled mutation-agent pairs.
Results

The framework identified three predicted structural and binding patterns. Variants directly affecting the C24-C37 or C28-C41 disulfide bonds showed the broadest predicted extracellular-domain and therapeutic-interface perturbation. The non-cysteine P23delins9 variant was also predicted to cause substantial backbone and interface remodeling, whereas C8-C21 disulfide-bond alterations and non-cysteine epitope variants showed agent-dependent predicted binding effects. In the two index patients, predictions for the therapies received were directionally concordant with progression.
Conclusions

Structural interpretation of TNFRSF17 variants may help prioritize newly identified variants for agent-specific functional evaluation. Direct disulfide-cysteine alterations were associated with broader predicted structural perturbation, non-cysteine variants more often showed agent-dependent effects. Prospective functional and clinical validation is required.

papers.t: Dynamic biomarkers of kidney function in patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma receiving daratumumab-based combination therapy
Impact of granulocyte colony-stimulating factors on cytokine release syndrome during bispecific antibody initiation in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma
papers.c: There was a trend towards increased risk of CRS after G-CSF exposure, although not significant (hazard ratio [HR] 1.7, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.6-4.7, p = 0.3). These results suggest that G-CSF administration can be considered for neutropenia during BsAb initiation.
ab: Bispecific antibody (BsAb) treatment in multiple myeloma can be associated with adverse events including cytokine release syndrome (CRS), cytopenias, and infections. While granulocyte colony-stimulating factors (G-CSF) can be used to treat neutropenia, little is known about their safety during the BsAb initiation period and whether G-CSF can increase the risk of CRS. To assess the impact of G-CSF on risk of CRS, we included all patients with multiple myeloma who received at least one dose (step-up doses [SUD] and first treatment dose [FTD]), of commercial teclistamab, elranatamab, or talquetamab between November 2022 and April 2024 at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (N = 186). Exposure to G-CSF was defined as administration of at least one dose of filgrastim from 48 h before up to 7 days after BsAb SUD or FTD, or one dose of peg-filgrastim between 7 days prior to up to 7 days after BsAb SUD or FTD. Of the 186 patients, 22 were classified as G-CSF exposed. CRS occurred in 16/22 (73%) patients with G-CSF exposure vs 76/164 (46%) of non-exposed. All CRS was grade 1 (56%) or grade 2 (44%) and the majority occurred prior to G-CSF was given (16/22 patients). The median absolute neutrophil count (ANC) at time of G-CSF exposure was 0.5 × 109/L (0.4-0.7). There was a trend towards increased risk of CRS after G-CSF exposure, although not significant (hazard ratio [HR] 1.7, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.6-4.7, p = 0.3). These results suggest that G-CSF administration can be considered for neutropenia during BsAb initiation.

papers.t: Increased Overall Survival for Subcutaneous Versus Intravenous Daratumumab in Medicare Beneficiaries With Multiple Myeloma
papers.c: Overall, Dara PH20 SC was associated with improved rwOS versus Dara IV in Medicare beneficiaries with MM, which appears to be driven by lower risk of serious infections and longer treatment duration with Dara PH20 SC.
ab: Background
Daratumumab has improved survival outcomes for patients with multiple myeloma (MM), but the effect of administration route on rwOS remains unclear.
Methods

Data from Medicare fee-for-service (January 2005-December 2024) and Medicare Advantage (January 2015-December 2022) were used. Eligible patients enrolled in Medicare aged ≥ 65 years were continuously enrolled in Parts A, B, and D for ≥ 12 months before daratumumab initiation. Patients were propensity-score matched with residual covariate adjustment. The primary end point was rwOS (time from index to death from any cause), assessed using Kaplan-Meier analyses, log-rank tests, and Cox models. Exploratory competing-risk analyses evaluated non-fatal events.
Results

Among 14,618 eligible patients (8324 SC; 6294 IV), 1191 patients per arm were well matched after propensity-score matching. Dara PH20 SC was associated with reduced all-cause mortality versus Dara IV (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.76, 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.67-0.86, P < .001) and lower risks of serious infections (HR: 0.87, 95% CI, 0.78-0.97, P < .01) and treatment discontinuation (HR: 0.72, 95% CI, 0.66-0.79, P < .01).
Conclusion

Overall, Dara PH20 SC was associated with improved rwOS versus Dara IV in Medicare beneficiaries with MM, which appears to be driven by lower risk of serious infections and longer treatment duration with Dara PH20 SC.

papers.t: Bone recovery after treatment study: Evidence of myeloma bone disease repair and partial microenvironment recovery
papers.c: However, bone lesion resolution is rare, potentially impaired by poor lacunar network connectivity. These data highlight the ongoing need for novel, bone-targeted therapies to support MBD recovery.
ab: Myeloma bone disease (MBD) affects ~90% of myeloma patients, causing pain and reduced quality of life. Current anti-resorptive treatments retard further destruction but do not repair bone. As new myeloma therapies emerge, understanding their impact on MBD is crucial. This pilot study assessed the feasibility of longitudinally measuring bone recovery in newly diagnosed myeloma patients receiving first-line therapy (e.g. induction ± autologous stem cell transplant, plus zoledronic acid), as a prelude to formally assessing bone anabolic strategies. Patients underwent whole-body low-dose computed tomography imaging and bone marrow biopsy at baseline and 3 months post-induction/autograft, alongside monthly bone turnover markers. All patients had evidence of partial osteolytic lesion repair, with one patient having resolution of some lesions. Trephine analysis revealed increased trabecular bone volume (p = 0.003) and osteoblast number (p < 0.05). However, osteocyte canalicular coverage was significantly reduced (p < 0.01). Serum C‑terminal telopeptide of type I collagen was suppressed from 2 months (p < 0.0001), and sclerostin from 3 months (p = 0.011). This pilot confirms the study design to be feasible. Results suggest that osteolytic lesions have the potential for partial repair, possibly supported by proteasome inhibitors. However, bone lesion resolution is rare, potentially impaired by poor lacunar network connectivity. These data highlight the ongoing need for novel, bone-targeted therapies to support MBD recovery.

papers.t: Bispecific antibodies targeting B-cell maturation antigen in multiple myeloma: Current clinical applications, challenges and future directions
papers.c: Finally, the use of bsAbs beyond multiple myeloma has been explored by reviewing clinical trials and real-world experiences in other monoclonal gammopathies (e.g., smoldering multiple myeloma and light-chain amyloidosis) or other conditions, such as autoimmune diseases. Overall, the objective of this review was to provide a comprehensive overview on the role of BCMA-targeting bsAbs while discussing future developments in this field, including their use across different settings and combinations strategies, as well as the ongoing efforts to improve safety and tolerability through the implementation of specific guidelines for toxicity management.
ab: Anti-B cell maturation antigen (BCMA) therapies, including antibody-drug conjugates, chimeric antigen receptor T cells, and bispecific antibodies (bsAbs), have recently revolutionized the treatment landscape of multiple myeloma. This review outlines the biologic rationale for targeting BCMA and sheds light on the mechanism of action of bsAbs and the main reasons behind loss of response and treatment resistance. Moreover, available safety and efficacy information on approved agents (i.e., teclistamab, elranatamab, and linvoseltamab) are described, focusing on the most relevant treatment-related toxicities, including cytokine release syndrome, immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, cytopenias, and infections, and established approaches for their monitoring and management. Furthermore, available data on active trials evaluating the use of bsAbs in combination with other agents and/or in earlier lines of therapy are discussed, as well as emerging data on novel anti-BCMA bsAbs in clinical development, such as etentamig. Finally, the use of bsAbs beyond multiple myeloma has been explored by reviewing clinical trials and real-world experiences in other monoclonal gammopathies (e.g., smoldering multiple myeloma and light-chain amyloidosis) or other conditions, such as autoimmune diseases. Overall, the objective of this review was to provide a comprehensive overview on the role of BCMA-targeting bsAbs while discussing future developments in this field, including their use across different settings and combinations strategies, as well as the ongoing efforts to improve safety and tolerability through the implementation of specific guidelines for toxicity management.

papers.t: Integration of peripheral blood lymphocyte subsets and cytokines enhances prognostic stratification in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma
papers.c: The model was deployed as an exploratory online calculator for convenience. These findings require independent external multicentre validation before implementation.
ab: Immune dysregulation is involved in multiple myeloma (MM) pathogenesis and progression yet current staging systems do not incorporate indicators of immune status. We retrospectively included 260 newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM) patients with baseline data of peripheral blood (PB) lymphocyte subsets and cytokines from Tianjin Medical University General Hospital. Through majority voting across seven survival prediction algorithms and subsequent Cox analysis, cluster of differentiation (CD)3+CD8+ T-cell absolute count and interleukin (IL-10) were identified as immune prognostic predictors to construct the immune risk score. A comprehensive prognostic nomogram was subsequently established by combining this score with high-risk cytogenetic abnormalities, serum calcium and serum lactate dehydrogenase. Shapley additive explanation analysis ranked the immune risk score as the leading contributor to the final model. The nomogram achieved a cross-validated 3-year time-dependent area under the curve for overall survival (OS) of 0.825. The model was further evaluated in a temporal validation cohort. In exploratory analyses within our cohort, the nomogram showed better prognostic performance than the established staging systems and further stratified outcomes among patients receiving anti-CD38 antibody-containing regimens. The model was deployed as an exploratory online calculator for convenience. These findings require independent external multicentre validation before implementation.

ab: The IMS-IMWG 2025 updated definition of high-risk multiple myeloma (HRMM) introduced next-generation sequencing (NGS) based detection of TP53 single-nucleotide variants (SNV) as an independent high-risk factor. However, most published data on TP53 SNVs in MM derive from exploratory research studies using NGS interpretation pipelines outside of quality-controlled, clinically accredited laboratories, with limited information on co-occurring high-risk cytogenetic abnormalities (HRCA). To address this, we retrospectively reviewed all transplant-eligible newly diagnosed MM (NDMM) patients treated at the Royal Marsden Hospital in the UK between February 2021 and April 2026 who underwent standard-of-care parallel fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) testing for all IMS-IMWG consensus genomic staging (CGS) criteria and NGS-based TP53 SNV calling in the National Health Service diagnostically accredited Genomic Laboratory Hub (GLH). A total of 102 patients were included. Based on FISH, 24 patients (23.5%) fulfilled IMS-IMWG CGS criteria for HRMM, including 8 (7.8%) with del(17p) and 5 (4.9%) with biallelic del(1p32). All 24 patients had co-occurrence of 2+ HRCA, including all 5 patients with biallelic del(1p32). NGS identified 4 cases (3.9%) with TP53 mutations, of which 2 harbored del(17p), while 2 were classified as HRMM solely based on NGS results. However, both isolated TP53mut also carried additional HRCA. Thus, in this standard-of-care diagnostic setting, only 2% of NDMM were re-classified based on NGS findings and, notably, all 26 HRMM had 2+ high-risk lesions. Although limited by cohort size and lack of survival outcomes, these descriptive data demonstrate genomic co-occurrence rather than independent prognostic value and support a continued focus on reliable, quality-controlled detection of structural variants alongside NGS.

papers.t: Discordant marrow MRD and PET-CT in myeloma: A four-state language for joint reporting
papers.c: This distinction matters for defining deep response, interpreting MRD-driven end-points and designing studies of response-adapted treatment. A four-state language turns discordance from an ambiguous finding into a reportable response framework.
ab: In a Nutshell, discordant bone marrow measurable residual disease (BM-MRD) and positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) assessments in multiple myeloma do not simply represent assay disagreement. They can provide clinically relevant information because the direction of discordance changes the interpretation of response: BM-MRD-negative/PET-positive disease indicates PET-visible disease outside the sampled marrow compartment, whereas BM-MRD-positive/PET-negative disease reflects marrow persistence without PET-visible disease. This distinction matters for defining deep response, interpreting MRD-driven end-points and designing studies of response-adapted treatment. A four-state language turns discordance from an ambiguous finding into a reportable response framework.
